blocked.system: Enter and verify the setup token to continue.
blocked.auth: Complete the administrator details to continue.

already.title: Application already configured
already.text: The initial setup has already been completed. Sign in with your account.

welcome.text: This guided procedure configures Scarlet in a few minutes. You can go back to previous steps at any time.
points: connection to Kubernetes and Podman (both optional)
monitoring with Prometheus (optional) and backup retention
welcome.demo: The application is in DEMO mode: Kubernetes and Podman are simulated and their settings are not saved.

token.text: For security you need the one-time token shown at the end of the installation (install.sh). If you no longer have it, generate a new one on the server with:
token.label: Setup token
token.invalid: Invalid token. Make sure you copied it entirely or generate a new one.
token.rateLimited: Too many attempts. Retry in {{seconds}} seconds.

system.title: System check
system.optionalNote: Warnings do not block the installation: you can fix them later.

os.warn: {{name}}: not Oracle Linux 9; the application can work but it is not the reference platform.

python.fail: Python {{version}}: version 3.11 or later is required.

data_dir.fail: {{path}} is not writable by the service user.

disk_space.warn: Only {{freeBytes}} free: backups may run out of space.

tls.ok: HTTPS active (direct TLS or reverse proxy).
tls.warn: HTTPS not active: in production configure a certificate (TLS step).

mode.warn: DEMO mode: simulated data, do not use in production.

k8s.text: Scarlet reads and manages the cluster with the credentials of a kubeconfig on the server. Recommended: a dedicated "pkm" ServiceAccount (deploy/kubernetes/pkm-rbac.yaml) with a kubeconfig in /etc/pkm/kubeconfig readable by the pkm user.
k8s.inCluster: Scarlet runs as a Pod in the cluster (uses the Pod service account)
k8s.kubeconfigHint: Path on the server (not on your PC).
k8s.contextHint: Empty = current context of the file.
k8s.optional: You can skip this step and configure Kubernetes later from Settings → Kubernetes.

podman.text: Scarlet manages the Podman containers of this host through the Podman API socket. For system containers enable the socket with: sudo systemctl enable --now podman.socket
podman.rootWarning: Whoever can use the rootful Podman socket effectively has root access to the host: the installer grants access only to the pkm group.

auth.text: Create the first Administrator account. You can add other users with Operator or Viewer roles from Security → Users.
auth.note: The password is stored only as an Argon2id hash: nobody, not even the server administrator, can read it.
auth.errUsername: Use letters, digits and . _ @ - (2 to 63 characters).

monitoring.text: Current CPU and memory usage comes from metrics-server, if installed in the cluster. Prometheus is optional and adds history, network traffic and volume usage. Without Prometheus Scarlet does not invent metrics: it shows "Advanced metrics not configured".
monitoring.urlHint: It must be reachable from the Scarlet server. Leave empty if you do not use Prometheus.

backup.text: Every night the pkm-backup.timer creates an archive with:
contents: the Scarlet database (users, audit log, settings, notifications)
optionally the YAML export of Kubernetes application resources (without Secrets)
backup.notCluster: It is not a backup of the Kubernetes cluster: it does not include etcd or persistent volume data. That requires dedicated tools (etcd snapshots, Velero).
backup.retentionHint: Older archives are deleted automatically. Directory: {{dir}}.
backup.timer: You can run a backup at any time from Operations → Backup or with: sudo pkm-admin backup

tls.offText: The connection is not encrypted: do not use this configuration in production.
tls.text: The installer generates a self-signed certificate in /etc/pkm/tls. To replace it with your company certificate copy the files and restart the service:
tls.commands:
sudo cp server.crt /etc/pkm/tls/pkm.crt
sudo cp server.key /etc/pkm/tls/pkm.key
sudo chown root:pkm /etc/pkm/tls/pkm.*
sudo chmod 0640 /etc/pkm/tls/pkm.key
sudo systemctl restart pkm
tls.proxy: Alternatively you can publish Scarlet behind an HTTPS reverse proxy (see INSTALL.md).

summary.text: Check your choices. Kubernetes, Podman, Prometheus and backup settings can be changed later from Settings.
summary.demoNote: In DEMO mode Kubernetes and Podman settings are not saved.

testStep.text: Check the configured connections one last time. Unreachable components do not block the installation.
testStep.nonBlocking: You can complete the installation even if a test fails and fix it later.

complete.text: Press the button to create the administrator and save the configuration. The setup token will be invalidated.

done.title: Installation completed
done.text: The account {{user}} has been created. Sign in to start using the console.

test.promOk: Prometheus answers in {{ms}} ms, {{targets}} monitored targets.
test.k8sHint: Check that the file exists and is readable by the pkm user, that the server is reachable (firewall, port 6443) and that certificate and token are valid.
test.podmanHint: Check that podman.socket is active (systemctl status podman.socket) and that the pkm group can access the socket.

reason.no_kubeconfig: No kubeconfig given: enter the path of the file on the server or skip this step.
reason.path_not_absolute: The path "{{path}}" is not absolute: enter the full path on the server, e.g. /etc/pkm/kubeconfig.
reason.file_not_found: The file "{{path}}" does not exist on the server. Copy it to the server (e.g. /etc/pkm/kubeconfig) or generate it with scripts/make-kubeconfig.sh.
reason.not_readable: The pkm user cannot read "{{path}}". Fix the permissions: sudo chown root:pkm {{path}} && sudo chmod 0640 {{path}}
reason.invalid_file: The file "{{path}}" is not a valid kubeconfig (see the detail below).
